# @uptimizr/agent-core

> The framework-agnostic, browser-safe core for Uptimizr analytics agents: the single read-only
> analytics tool catalog over the collector query API, the `annotate`-gated project-metadata tools,
> a headless LLM provider-adapter interface, and the tool-calling loop. Defined once, consumed by
> MCP, the dashboard, and the demo (ADR 0050). Events are read-only (ADR 0051 §9).

## Docs

- [Package reference](./README.md): install, usage, the full tool table, and the programmatic API.
- [Agent guide](./AGENTS.md): rules and tool catalog for AI agents.
- [Integration & API reference](https://github.com/RaananW/Uptimizr/blob/main/docs/integration.md): the underlying query endpoints.
- [Architecture Decision Records](https://github.com/RaananW/Uptimizr/tree/main/docs/adr): in-browser assistant (0050), privacy model (0003), thin backends (0005), consumer-facing agents (0017).

## The `query` tool (the query DSL)

`query` is the one tool that is not per-metric (ADR 0051 §3): its input is the query DSL, so it runs
any metric above with any filter that metric declares —
`{ "v": 1, "metric": "mesh_sources", "range": { "since": …, "until": … }, "filters": { "scene": "lobby" }, "format": "summary" }`.
`range` is required, `format` defaults to `table`, and a metric/dimension/filter outside the
registry's vocabulary returns a `400` whose `issues[].accepted` names what would have worked.
`compare`, `segment`, `order`, `explain`, `filters.event` and `filters.device` parse but are not
answered yet. It travels as `GET /api/v1/query?q=<url-encoded JSON>`.
`hover_dwell`, `interaction_sources`, `top_input_actions`, `camera_gestures`, `navigation_stats`,
`backtrack_ratio`, `perf_summary`, `render_scale_truth`, `perf_distribution`, `fps_histogram`,
`frame_time_percentiles`, `jank_rate`, `perf_churn`, `perf_by_device`, `perf_by_scene`,
`perf_heatmap`, `compile_stalls`, `resource_summary`, `resource_percentiles`, `stability_counts`,
`graphics_diagnostics`, `error_heatmap`, `rendering_technology`, `capability_changes`,
`xr_rotation`, `xr_sources`, `xr_abandonment`, `xr_locomotion`, `xr_tracking_quality`,
`boundary_heatmap`, `boundary_heatmap_stats`, `xr_boundary_contacts`,
`ar_placement_time_to_place`, `ar_placement_attempts`, `ar_placement_surfaces`, `funnel`,

## Insight primitives (ADR 0051 §4)

Three of the tools are readings *about* the other metrics, and they are the right first call on an
Four of the tools are readings *about* the other metrics, and they are the right first call on an
open-ended question — "how are things?" does not mean "call thirty tools".

- `insight_scene_health` — one 0-100 score per scene over six weighted factors (perf stability,
  jank, errors, dead clicks, coverage, XR abandonment), least healthy first. The right *unscoped*
  starting point: it answers which scene to open. Every factor carries the `metric` id behind it,
  its `raw` value and the project `baseline` it was compared with, so the next call and the
  sentence to write are both already in the row. **50 is the project norm, not a pass mark** — the
  score compares a scene with the rest of the project's recent past — and a factor with
  `score: null` was not counted (its `note` says why).
- `insight_movers` — what changed against a reference window (the previous equal one by default),
  for every comparable metric in scope, ranked by a robust z-score: the change divided by how much
  that metric normally swings, so a noisy metric must move much further than a steady one to reach
  the top. Bounded: at most 24 metrics are scanned per request.
- `insight_baseline` — what is normal for one metric in one scene: `median` and `mad`, the
  `p10`..`p90` band, and the drift `slope`. Call it on whatever moved, to say whether the new level
  is actually outside normal rather than merely different.
- `insight_anomalies` — *when* one metric went wrong. One row per bucket that does not belong in
  the series: `kind: "spike" | "drop"` for a bucket more than `sensitivity` (default 3) standard
  deviations from the trailing window, and `kind: "shift"` at the bucket where the level moved and
  stayed moved. Where the metric declares a dimension it can be split by, `contributor` names the
  mesh, source, input action, event type or scene holding the largest `share` of the excess.
  Bounded: one scan for the series plus at most three attribution scans per request.

Read `insight_anomalies`' `z` as standard deviations and `insight_movers`' as the same ratio
unscaled — they differ by a constant factor (1.4826) and must not be compared directly. A sustained
level change is reported both as a `shift` and, for the days right after it, as `drop`/`spike`
rows: two true statements about one event.
- `insight_significance` — whether a difference between two windows could be chance: `effect`,
  `ci95`, `p`, and the `test` that produced them (a two-proportion z with Wilson intervals for a
  declared rate, Welch's t over the per-bucket values for a level, an exact Poisson rate test for a
  bare count — picked from the measure, not from you). **Read `ci95` before `p`**: an interval that
  straddles 0 means you cannot tell yet, and `powerNote` says what this much data could have
  detected at all. Welch's `n` is the number of **buckets**, not events. It compares two *windows*,
  not two segments: a variant-versus-variant question is a `400`, not a wrong answer.

Two fields decide whether a mover is worth reporting, and both are easy to misread:

- `direction` is the registry's opinion of what a **rise** in that metric means — `up` (good),
  `down` (bad) or `neutral`. It is *not* the direction of the move: read it with the sign of
  `delta`, so a rise in a `down` metric (errors, dead clicks, jank) is a regression.
- `aboveMinSample: false` means the delta is real arithmetic but the denominator is below the
  metric's declared minimum. Such rows are returned rather than dropped — "we cannot tell" and
  "nothing changed" are different answers — and must never be reported as findings.

Statistics are computed in pure TypeScript over portable day/hour buckets, so the same data yields
the same answer on every storage engine. Only `comparable` metrics with a faithful per-bucket form
participate; asking for one that has none returns `400` naming every id that does.

## Result formats (`format`)

Every aggregate tool declares a `format` argument — the envelope its rows arrive in, not a filter
(ADR 0051 §2). `buildRequest` applies `DEFAULT_TOOL_FORMAT` (`table`) when the caller names none
and sends it explicitly, so the collector's own default stays `full`. A tool's output schema
describes all three envelopes, so whichever one comes back validates.

- `summary` — **prefer this whenever a model reads the result.** A bounded digest: `ranked` top
  rows, a `series` trend, merged spatial `clusters`, or a single `record`, with shares, a sample
  size, the metric's `caveats` and a templated `reading` sentence. Capped at the metric's
  `limits.maxSummaryRows`, so a 500-bin heatmap costs the same as a 5-bin one — which is what keeps
  one heatmap from filling a small local model's whole context.
- `table` — **the tools' default.** `{ meta, rows }`: every row plus the metric, range, applied
  filters, sample size, row count, a truncation flag and the registry limits. Self-describing but
  not bounded — ask for `summary` when the result could be large.
- `full` — the bare rows, with no envelope at all.

`reading` and `caveats` are templated by pure code, never a model, so identical rows always produce
identical words. Shares appear only where the measure can honestly be summed (an FPS or ratio metric
reports `total: null` and no shares). Cluster coordinates are grid indices — multiply by the
effective `cellSize` for world space. `session_meta` and `scene_representation` are stored records,
not aggregations, and declare no `format`.

## Key exports

- `readTools` — the read-only tool catalog (one entry per query endpoint), generated from the
  `@uptimizr/metrics` metric registry: 69 tools, each with an input schema, an output schema
  covering all three `format` envelopes, and the metric's interpretation notes and caveats in its
  description (ADR 0051).
- `writeTools` / `mutatingWriteTools` — the project-metadata tools `annotate`, `define_term`,
  `save_analysis` plus `list_annotations`, `list_glossary`, `list_analyses` (ADR 0051 §5). A
  separate export from `readTools` on purpose, so an integration's read-only stance stays
  inspectable. They need an `annotate` key, write metadata only, and cannot touch an event.
  `@uptimizr/metrics` metric registry: 70 tools, each with an input schema, an output schema and the
  metric's interpretation notes and caveats in its description (ADR 0051).
- `coreReadTools` / `selectReadTools(kind)` / `filterReadTools(names)` — narrowed views of the
  catalog for models that cannot carry every tool schema.
- `registryToTools(metrics?)` — generate the catalog from metric-registry definitions.
- `createCollectorClient(config)` — the thin collector client: `get` for every analytics read, plus
  `post`/`put`/`delete` used only by the metadata write tools.
- `runAgent(options)` — the headless tool-calling loop (LLM ↔ tools ↔ collector).
- `toToolSchemas(tools?)` — convert catalog tools to JSON-Schema tool descriptors for an LLM.
- `renderContextForPrompt(context, nowMs?)` — render the collector's project context document
  (`GET /api/v1/context`, ADR 0051 §5) as a compact system-prompt block: the project's real scene
  ids, named region ids, custom-event names with their prop keys and coarse types, top meshes, input
  actions, data freshness, retention flags and the metrics that are empty because their capture
  channel is off. Pure, ~1.5 k characters at most, tolerant of a partial document, and `""` when
  there is nothing to say — so an older collector degrades instead of failing. Read the context
  first and inject this before the first question.
- `AGENT_SKILLS` / `getAgentSkill(name)` / `renderAgentSkill(name, args)` — the curated
  investigations (`weekly_scene_health`, `attention_hotspots`, `xr_comfort_review`): title,
  description, the registry tools each method relies on, its arguments, and a pure `render(args)`
  producing the user turn. `@uptimizr/mcp` registers them as prompt templates and
  `uptimizr agent report --skill` runs them headlessly, from this one definition. The resolver is a
  function so packaged `SKILL.md` skills can plug in later without changing consumers.
- `ANALYTICS_AGENT_GUIDELINES` / `renderCurrentTimeLine(nowMs)` — the system-prompt fragments every
  analytics agent shares (what it may claim about the data; the clock it resolves "this week"
  against). Clients add only their own role sentence and output format.
- `LlmProvider` — the pluggable, user-controlled LLM backend interface (no bundled model or key).
- `ProviderResponse.usage` — optional `{ inputTokens?, outputTokens? }` per turn, populated by the
  hosted adapters from Anthropic's `usage` and OpenAI's `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`
  (buffered and streamed). Absent means **not reported**, never zero.

## Capability-gated tools (ADR 0051 §7)

- `readTools` is the `query` surface; `rawTools` holds the tools whose registry endpoint declares `capability: "query:raw"` (today `session_narrative`, the compacted account of one session).
- Keep them apart: the capability belongs to the key the agent was handed. Register `rawTools` only after `GET /api/v1/whoami` confirms `query:raw` — the collector also requires `ENABLE_RAW_SESSION_RETENTION`, so the capability is necessary but not sufficient (ADR 0003).

## Non-metric reads

- `list_subscriptions` — the project's conditional subscriptions (ADR 0051 §6). Not a registry
  metric: configuration, not a measurement. No arguments, no time range. Creating/deleting one
  needs `annotate` and is not a tool.
